title: Public-coin upper bound for equality by hashing
statement:
Fix natural numbers $n$ and $k$ and a real number $\varepsilon$ satisfying $1/2^{k} < \varepsilon$. Then the $\varepsilon$-error public-coin randomized communication complexity of the equality function $\mathrm{equality}_n$ on pairs of $n$-bit Boolean strings satisfies
\[
  \mathrm{R}^{\mathrm{pub}}_{\varepsilon}(\mathrm{equality}_n) \;\le\; k + 1,
\]
where the bound is taken in the extended naturals $\bbn \cup \{\infty\}$.
replaced:
If $\varepsilon > 0$ and $1/2^k < \varepsilon$, then the public-coin
communication complexity of $\mathrm{equality}_n$ with error at most $\varepsilon$
satisfies
\[
  R_\varepsilon(\mathrm{equality}_n) \;\le\; k + 1.
\]
